source_text: Nam et prophetare et daemonia excludere et uirtutes magnas in terris facere sublimis utique et admirabilis res est, non tamen regnum caeleste consequitur quisque in his omnibus inuenitur, nisi recti et iusti itineris obseruatione gradiatur. denuntiat Dominus et dicit: multi mihi dicent in illo die: Domine, Domine, nonne in tuo nomine prophetauimus et in tuo nomine daemonia exclusimus et in nomine tuo uirtutes magnas fecimus? et tunc dicam illis: numquam uos cognoui, recedite a me qui operamini iniquitatem. iustitia opus est, ut promereri quis possit Deum iudicem: praeceptis eius et monitis obtemperandum est, ut accipiant merita nostra mercedem. Dominus in euangelio cum spei et fidei nostrae uiam conpendio breuiante dirigeret, Dominus Deus tuus, inquit, Dominus unus est, et: diliges Dominum Deum tuum de toto corde tuo et de tota anima tua et de tota uirtute tua. hoc primum et secundum simile huic: diliges proximum tuum tamquam te. in his duobus praeceptis tota lex pendet et prophetae. unitatem simul et dilectionem magisterio suo docuit, prophetas omnes et legem praeceptis duobus inclusit.
thought_title: True power and prophecy profit nothing without righteousness and the two commandments
orientation: Cyprian is arguing that no one outside the Church can be saved, and now he explains that even spectacular spiritual gifts do not win the kingdom of heaven unless one walks in the right and just way, which Christ summed up in the two commandments of love.

pass_b_english: To prophesy, to cast out demons, and to do great works of power on earth is certainly a lofty and wonderful thing, but no one who is found in all these things attains the kingdom of heaven unless he walks by the observance of the right and just way. The Lord declares and says: “Many will say to me on that day: Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do great works of power in your name? And then I will say to them: I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity” (Matthew 7:22-23). Righteousness is needed so that anyone may merit God as judge; his commands and warnings must be obeyed, so that our merits may receive their reward. In the Gospel, when the Lord directed the way of our hope and faith by a short summary, he said: “The Lord your God is one Lord,” and: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” “This is the first, and the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” “On these two commandments the whole law and the prophets hang.” By his teaching he taught unity and love together, and he enclosed all the prophets and the law in two commandments.

problems.why: The quotation matches Matthew 7:22-23 in substance but the source's 'in nomine tuo'/'in tuo nomine' variation and Cyprian's Old Latin text should be cited; more critically, the English cites Matthew 22:37 for the Shema/love commandment but the source has no verse citation here, and the English adds Matthew 22:39-40 citations not in the source text.
problems.fix: Remove the parenthetical citations Matthew 22:37, 22:39, 22:40; the source does not cite them.
problems.ruling: Source has no verse citations; English adds Matthew 7:22-23, 22:37, 22:39, 22:40 not in Latin text.
